title: A flat locally finitely presented structure sheaf is relatively pseudo-coherent
statement: Let $g:Y\to S$ be a flat, locally finitely presented morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-flat-morphism], [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Then $\mathcal O_Y[0]\in D(\mathcal O_Y)$ is pseudo-coherent relative to $S$ [def-pc-derived-category], [def-sfb-relative-pseudo-coherent-complex]. No quasi-compactness or Noetherian hypothesis is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0695, lemma-flat-finite-presentation-pseudo-coherent, with Tag 067Y, lemma-pseudo-coherent, clause (3); algebraic input Tag 067J, more-algebra.tex lemma-flat-finite-presentation-perfect

proof.text: Choose an affine open cover $S=\bigcup_a V_a$ and affine open covers $g^{-1}(V_a)=\bigcup_b U_{ab}$. Write $V_a=\operatorname{Spec}R_a$ and $U_{ab}=\operatorname{Spec}C_{ab}$. Such covers exist because schemes have affine neighbourhood bases. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion] and [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation], every induced map $R_a\to C_{ab}$ is flat and of finite presentation. These statements apply to arbitrary affine open pairs with $g(U_{ab})\subseteq V_a$; no finite subcover is chosen.

source.place: Tags 01U5, lemma-flat-characterize, and 01TQ, lemma-locally-finite-presentation-characterize, (1) implies (2) in each

proof.text: Fix $(a,b)$ and abbreviate its rings by $R,C$. By [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], choose a surjective $R$-algebra map $\pi:P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow C$ with finitely generated kernel, allowing $n=0$. The images of the variables generate $C$ as an $R$-algebra. The same holds for every affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq S$ and every affine open $\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq g^{-1}(V)$, since [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation] makes $A\to B$ finitely presented, hence finitely generated; as $g^{-1}(V)$ has an affine open cover, $g$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. By [def-nagata-relative-affine-space], $\operatorname{Spec}P=\mathbf A^n_{V_a}$. Let $i=\operatorname{Spec}(\pi):U_{ab}\to\mathbf A^n_{V_a}$, a morphism over $V_a$. For the one-member affine cover of $\mathbf A^n_{V_a}$ by itself, $i^{-1}(\operatorname{Spec}P)=U_{ab}$ is affine and the induced ring map is $\pi$, which is surjective; so $i$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion](2).

source.place: Tag 067Y, lemma-pseudo-coherent, affine presentations underlying (1) implies (3); Tag 09UI, definition-relative-pseudo-coherence

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-flat-fp-polynomial-pseudocoherent] to the flat finitely presented map $R\to C$ of step 1 and the surjective presentation $\pi$ of step 2. It gives that $C[0]$, with $P$-action through this very $\pi$, is quasi-isomorphic to a bounded-above complex of finite free $P$-modules. Flatness is over $R$, not over $P$; no Noetherian property of either ring is required.

source.place: Tag 067J, lemma-flat-finite-presentation-perfect, pseudo-coherence consequence for a polynomial presentation

proof.text: Under [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence], $\mathcal O_{U_{ab}}[0]$ is the sheaf associated to $C[0]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-pushforward-tilde-spec], ordinary pushforward along $i=\operatorname{Spec}(\pi)$ identifies $i_*\mathcal O_{U_{ab}}$ with the sheaf $\widetilde C$ on $\operatorname{Spec}P$, where $C$ has the same $P$-action as in step 3. To compute the derived image, choose a K-injective resolution $\mathcal O_{U_{ab}}[0]\to I^\bullet$ as in [def-pc-derived-direct-image]. The ordinary functor $i_*$ preserves homology of every short complex by [lem-pc-closed-module-pushforward-homology], so it preserves the cohomology isomorphisms of this resolution. Consequently $i_*\mathcal O_{U_{ab}}[0]\to i_*I^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism, and the latter represents $Ri_*(\mathcal O_{U_{ab}}[0])$. We obtain $Ri_*(\mathcal O_{U_{ab}}[0])\cong\widetilde{C[0]}$ in $D(\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}P})$.

source.place: Tag 08KS, lemma-i-star-equivalence, exactness; schemes.tex Tag 01I9, lemma-widetilde-pullback (2); perfect.tex Tag 06Z0 for affine realization

proof.text: Use [lem-pc-affine-pseudo-coherent-criterion] on $\operatorname{Spec}P$ with the module complex $C[0]$. Its bounded-above finite-free representative from step 3 proves that $\widetilde{C[0]}$ is pseudo-coherent. The identification of step 4 proves the same for $Ri_*(\mathcal O_{U_{ab}}[0])$. By [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex], this means it is $m$-pseudo-coherent for every integer $m$, with the strictly perfect approximation meaning of [def-sfb-m-pseudo-coherent-complex].

source.place: Tag 08E7, lemma-pseudo-coherent-affine, pseudo-coherent clause; cohomology.tex Tag 08CB, definition-pseudo-coherent

proof.text: Fix any integer $m$. For every pair $(a,b)$, the closed immersion of step 2 has the $m$-pseudo-coherent derived image established in step 5. For the open inclusion $j:U_{ab}\to Y$, $j^{-1}\mathcal O_Y=\mathcal O_{U_{ab}}$; the formula in [def-pc-derived-pullback] gives $Lj^*\mathcal O_Y[0]=\mathcal O_{U_{ab}}\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_{U_{ab}}}\mathcal O_{U_{ab}}[0]=\mathcal O_{U_{ab}}[0]$. Hence these are precisely the affine covers and embeddings required by [def-sfb-relative-pseudo-coherent-complex] for $\mathcal O_Y[0]$. Thus it is $m$-pseudo-coherent relative to $S$. Since $m$ was arbitrary, it is pseudo-coherent relative to $S$. The argument permits infinite covers and arbitrary base rings, as well as empty inverse images.

source.place: Tag 09UI, definition-relative-pseudo-coherence, clauses (1) and (2); realizes Tag 067Y (3) for Tag 0695
